content.value_statement: Long-form writing often stalls when research, structure, citations, and revision happen in separate steps. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through outlining, source gathering, drafting feedback, and final polish.
actual_capabilities: Creates collaborative outlines for articles, newsletters, tutorials, and thought leadership pieces.
Identifies research gaps and adds citation tasks to an outline.
Suggests stronger hooks based on audience, topic, and desired tone.
Reviews draft sections for clarity, flow, evidence, style, and voice fit.
Formats citations as inline references, numbered references, or footnotes.
Provides final draft reviews with polish suggestions and a publication checklist.
limitations: It depends on available sources and user-provided context for factual accuracy.
It cannot guarantee that cited claims are correct without source verification.
It does not publish content to a CMS or manage editorial calendars.
It needs writing samples to preserve a specific personal or brand voice.

use_cases.title: Plan a Blog Article
use_cases.description: Create an outline, define research needs, and draft a stronger introduction before writing the full article.

use_cases.title: Build a Technical Tutorial
use_cases.description: Organize tutorial steps, add explanations, check clarity, and prepare troubleshooting notes for readers.

use_cases.title: Refine Thought Leadership
use_cases.description: Develop a clear thesis, strengthen evidence, preserve voice, and polish a complete draft for publication.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Outline
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a new article or newsletter.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create an outline for a [length] piece about [topic] for [audience]. Ask questions before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Research Key Claims
prompt_templates.scenario: Add evidence before drafting body sections.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research the claims in my outline and list credible sources, useful data, and citation gaps for each section.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Hook
prompt_templates.scenario: Strengthen the opening of an existing draft.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this introduction for clarity, curiosity, and audience fit. Suggest three stronger hooks in my voice.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Full Draft
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a finished draft for publication.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my full draft for structure, evidence, tone, citations, and readiness. Return prioritized edits and a final checklist.

output_examples.input: Outline an article about AI in product management for senior product leaders.
output: A structured outline with hook, introduction, three body sections, conclusion, and research tasks.
Research gaps for adoption data, workflow examples, and risks for product teams.
Questions about audience, desired stance, and publication length.

output_examples.input: Review my common mistakes section and make it more useful.
output: Specific feedback on clarity, flow, evidence, and tone.
Suggested line edits for vague statements and weak transitions.
Recommendations for data, examples, and section order.

output_examples.input: Prepare my finished newsletter for publication.
output: A final review of structure, readability, citations, and consistency.
A short list of high-priority edits before publishing.
A pre-publish checklist for claims, links, formatting, and proofreading.

best_practices: Share the target audience, goal, format, length, and tone before asking for an outline.
Verify every citation against the original source before publishing.
Provide writing samples when voice preservation matters.
anti_patterns: Asking the skill to invent citations or statistics without source checks.
Requesting a full rewrite before defining audience, thesis, or constraints.
Accepting polished text without reviewing facts, tone, and legal risk.

faq.question: Can this skill write a full article for me?
faq.answer: Yes, it can help draft sections, but it works best when you guide the thesis, audience, and voice.

faq.question: Does it verify citations automatically?
faq.answer: It can organize and format citations, but you should confirm each source before publication.

faq.question: Can it preserve my writing style?
faq.answer: Yes, it asks for tone preferences and examples so revisions can stay close to your voice.

faq.question: What content formats does it support?
faq.answer: It supports articles, newsletters, tutorials, case studies, documentation, and thought leadership drafts.

faq.question: Is it useful for technical writing?
faq.answer: Yes, it can outline tutorials, improve explanations, add troubleshooting notes, and check reader flow.

faq.question: What should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the topic, target audience, goal, desired length, tone, and any sources you already trust.
